subject: What Changed to Your Credit Card Today? Edition 13
summary: ICICI narrows lounge access on the Parakram card and removes a spend gate on the Emirates Sapphiro, HSBC tweaks two benefits, and Axis Bank waives fees on two more cards.
body_html:
Today's the kind of day that makes the case for actually reading your card's terms page once in a while instead of trusting what you remember from when you signed up. ICICI moved lounge access rules on four different cards, one worse, one meaningfully better, and HSBC and Axis Bank both made smaller moves worth five minutes of your time.

Parakram Credit Card

This one's confirmed independently, not just read off ICICI's own page. The card's quarterly lounge benefit used to just say "Get 1 Airport Lounge access every quarter," no domestic or international qualifier, which most readers would take as flexible. Today it's been rewritten to "Get 1 Domestic Airport Lounge access," full stop.

If you were treating that quarterly visit as usable at an international lounge on a layover, it isn't anymore, at least not going by what ICICI's page now says, and three independent sources corroborate that this is a real, current change, not a scraping glitch.

The catch: if international lounge access was ever part of why you picked this card, it's domestic-only now. Check before your next trip abroad rather than finding out at the gate.

Emirates Sapphiro Credit Card

Good news for once, and this one's confirmed too. The domestic lounge benefit used to come with a condition: 2 visits a quarter, but only if you'd spent ₹75,000 or more on the card in the preceding quarter. That spend gate is gone. It now just reads "Get 2 Domestic Airport Lounge access," no threshold attached.

A single walk-in domestic lounge visit typically runs somewhere around ₹700 to ₹1,000 if you paid for it yourself. Two visits a quarter, four times a year, that's roughly ₹5,600 to ₹8,000 a year in lounge access you now get regardless of whether you cross ₹75,000 in spend that quarter. If your spending on this card is lumpy, big quarter, quiet quarter, you no longer lose the benefit in the quiet ones.

The catch: none that I can find, this is a straightforward benefit improvement with the gate removed, not tightened. If anything, the catch is trusting it. Verify at your next lounge visit that the desk isn't still checking the old spend threshold, banks are sometimes slower to update their lounge partner network than their website.

Emirates Emeralde Credit Card

The same Primary Cardholder wording narrowing I flagged on Times Black and Emeralde a couple of days ago has now shown up here too. "Unlimited" lounge access is split into international and domestic rows, both specified for the Primary Cardholder. This is the fourth ICICI premium card in three days carrying this exact wording change, which makes me more confident it's a deliberate, portfolio-wide copy update rather than a one-off, but I still can't confirm what it means in practice for add-on cardholders.

The catch: if you've got an add-on card on this account, this is the third card in a row I'd tell you to double check with ICICI directly rather than assume nothing's changed.

HSBC Taj Credit Card

Small, specific number change: the discount cap on Yatra flight bookings dropped from ₹10,500 to ₹10,000, still 20% off, just a lower ceiling. On a ₹50,000 flight booking, 20% off used to cap out at ₹10,500 in savings; now it caps at ₹10,000, a ₹500 difference. I'll flag that this shows up on HSBC's own page as of today, and I haven't found independent confirmation of it yet, so treat it as HSBC's own current copy rather than a fully corroborated fact.

The catch: ₹500 won't change your travel budget, but if you were about to book a big-ticket flight specifically banking on the old ₹10,500 cap, know the number's lower now.

Live+ Credit Card

A genuine small addition here. On top of the existing 2 domestic and 1 international lounge visits a year, HSBC's page now advertises a complimentary 1GB Global eSIM plus 20% off top-ups for this card. A 1GB global data eSIM alone typically runs somewhere in the ₹700 to ₹1,500 range depending on the destination, so this is a real, if modest, addition if you travel internationally even occasionally. I haven't seen this independently confirmed yet, so I'd treat it as HSBC's own current claim rather than a settled fact until you've actually activated one.

The catch: try activating the eSIM benefit before your next international trip rather than assuming it's live and ready. New benefit rollouts on bank cards sometimes lag the marketing copy by a few weeks.

FLIPKART AXIS BANK Credit Card

The ₹500 joining fee on this card has dropped to nil, marked as a limited period offer. The annual fee from the second year onwards is unchanged at ₹500, still waived if you cross ₹3,50,000 in spends that year. So the actual change here is simple: it costs you nothing to get the card right now, where it used to cost ₹500 up front.

The catch: "limited period offer" means exactly that. If you're planning to apply, don't sit on it assuming the fee waiver will still be there next month.

AXIS BANK PRIVILEGE Credit Card

This card stopped taking new applicants a while back, but if you're an existing holder, there's real money in today's change. The standard annual fee from the second year onwards, normally ₹1,500, is being waived, again marked as a limited period offer. That's ₹1,500 you weren't expecting to save on your next renewal. Add-on card fees were already nil and remain nil.

The catch: this is a card the bank isn't actively selling anymore, so don't expect this waiver to be advertised loudly. If your renewal is coming up, check your statement when it lands to make sure the ₹1,500 didn't sneak through anyway before the waiver caught up in their system.

What I'd actually do with this

If you hold the Parakram Credit Card and were counting on that quarterly lounge visit working internationally, it doesn't anymore, plan your next trip accordingly.

If you hold the Emirates Sapphiro, you no longer need to hit ₹75,000 a quarter to get your two domestic lounge visits. That's free money you were leaving on the table before if your spending was ever below that line.

If an add-on cardholder relies on lounge access on any Emirates Emeralde, Times Black, or Emeralde account, I'd stop waiting for ICICI to clarify on its own and just call them.

If you've been eyeing the Flipkart Axis Bank card, the joining fee is nil right now, that's as good a time as any to apply, just don't wait too long.

And if you already hold the Axis Bank Privilege card, watch your next renewal statement, ₹1,500 should not show up on it.

This is my honest read, not formal financial advice. I'm not your advisor, and before you act on anything here, run it past a professional or at least sleep on it. But this is exactly how I'd think about it if these were my cards.

Monzy
